subject: History
description: Covers INA and Partition of Bengal.

questions.stem: During the freedom struggle, who was the founder of the 'Indian National Army' (Azad Hind Fauj) in Singapore?
questions.explanation:
WHY IT IS CORRECT: While the idea of the INA was originally conceived by Captain Mohan Singh, it was properly organized, massively expanded, and led into battle by Netaji Subhas Chandra Bose after he arrived in Singapore in 1943. He famously gave the slogan "Give me blood, and I will give you freedom!"
DECOY BUSTING: Rash Behari Bose handed over the leadership of the Indian Independence League to Subhas. Bhagat Singh founded the HSRA in India, not the INA.
EXAM INSIGHT: The INA was unique for having an all-women's combat regiment named the 'Rani of Jhansi Regiment', led by Captain Lakshmi Sahgal.

questions.stem: In 1905, the controversial 'Partition of Bengal' was carried out by which British Viceroy?
questions.explanation:
WHY IT IS CORRECT: Lord Curzon divided the massive province of Bengal into two in 1905, ostensibly for administrative convenience. However, the real motive was to divide the Hindu and Muslim populations and weaken the growing nationalist movement in Bengal. This sparked the massive Swadeshi Movement.
DECOY BUSTING: Dalhousie is known for the Doctrine of Lapse and Railways (1853). Mountbatten oversaw the final partition of India (1947). Cornwallis introduced the Permanent Settlement.
EXAM INSIGHT: Due to massive, unrelenting protests, the British were forced to annul the partition of Bengal in 1911 during the Delhi Durbar, simultaneously shifting the capital from Calcutta to Delhi.
